messages:
liang_ml: quick heads-up — galileo-v2 (quant=q5) on staging produced some orthography/diacritic regressions across multiple locales, filing thread here for triage. repro+metrics below.

anya: what are the exact symptoms?

liang_ml: two main classes: 1) Hebrew niqqud (vowel points) shifting to the previous glyph (so vowel ends up attached to prior consonant), 2) Mandarin pinyin tone digits/marks concatenating to the following hanzi or to adjacent latin tokens (e.g., "ni3 hao3" -> "ni3hao3" or "nǐhǎo" collapsed). Also seen in mixed RTL+CJK strings where punctuation reflows oddly.

ryan_dev: can you paste a minimal input -> output example?

liang_ml: sure. run on staging with config used for smoke: `model=galileo-v2, quant=q5, seq_len=512, tokenizer=unified-v2`

Input:
```
he: שלום
zh: 你好
en: Hello
mix: שלום ni3 hao3 
```

Output (float16 baseline):
```
he: שָׁלוֹם
zh: 你好
en: Hello
mix: שָׁלוֹם ni3 hao3
```

Output (galileo-v2 q5 staging):
```
he: שָׁלֹם  <-- niqqud moved left
zh: 你好
en: Hello
mix: שָׁלוֹםni3hao3  <-- tones concatenated
```

liang_ml: quick eval numbers (multilingual-sanchuan test split, beam=4):
```
float16 baseline (galileo-v2 fp16): BLEU=24.7, chrF=46.2
galileo-v2 q5 (staging): BLEU=23.1, chrF=42.9
delta: BLEU -1.6, chrF -3.3
```

marta_prod: hmm sizable chrF hit for zh. Is this confined to q5 kernel selection/packing? did you try q5 with the old kernel flags?

liang_ml: I've run two quick variants: q5 + old-kernel-alloc -> matches baseline. q5 + new-pack -> reproduces regression. suspect packing reorder or subtoken merge during tokenization post-compile.

anya: could this be a tokenizer patch we shipped separately? any tokenizer version mismatch between fp16 and q5 builds?

liang_ml: tokenizer version is unified-v2 on both. compile-time flag `merge_subtokens=true` was toggled in the q5 build. reverting that flag fixes the symptoms in short smoke.

ryan_dev: please bisect commit/compile flags to confirm. also add failing prompts to a blacklist for canary until fixed. can you run `./run_eval.py --model galileo-v2 --quant q5 --compare fp16 --dataset multilingual-sanchuan --locales zh,he,ar --save-failures` and attach output?

liang_ml: running now, will paste artifact when done. early results posted by eval-bot below.

eval-bot: automated run complete: https://ci.internal/runs/4350001234 (artifacts: `fails.jsonl`, `metrics.json`)
Metrics summary:
- galileo-v2 fp16: BLEU=24.72, chrF=46.18
- galileo-v2 q5 (pack+merge_subtokens): BLEU=23.09, chrF=42.87
Top failing examples saved to `fails.jsonl` (100 samples, locales: zh/he/ar).

marta_prod: good. next steps: 1) eng-ml triage takes bisect on compile flags, 2) eng-runtime looks at packer kernel ordering, 3) add locale-specific smoke checks (Hebrew niqqud alignment + zh tone tokenization) to release gating. I'll open tickets. :eyes:

ryan_dev: tagging eng-runtime and tokenization owners. @eng-runtime @tokenizer-team please see artefacts.

liang_ml: opened issue: https://rwd/issues/2345 — contains failing prompts and a tiny repro harness (`repro_q5_niqqud.py`). I'll attach local patch that toggles `merge_subtokens` for q5 builds as a temporary mitigation.

anya: thanks. can we also run the same eval on `galileo-v2 q5-int8-compat` branch? want to know if int8 path shares the packer.

liang_ml: doing that next. will update thread when I have numbers.

marta_prod: if int8 is clean, consider shipping q5 with `merge_subtokens=false` until packer fix; add note to release docs.

liang_ml: ACK. posting short checklist I've started: 
- [ ] bisect compile flag -> who: liang_ml
- [ ] runtime packer audit -> who: eng-runtime
- [ ] add locale smoke tests -> who: marta_prod
- [ ] temporary revert `merge_subtokens` for q5 in canary -> who: liang_ml

ryan_dev: thanks team. small follow-up: include the exact token ids around the failing characters to help kernel folks (liang please paste token ids next).

liang_ml: will attach token-id dump in the issue. for now adding the `fails.jsonl` snippet to the issue.

anya: great triage. :thumbsup"
